# Architecture

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## Authoritative local game domain

### State and transitions

`model.game.manager.GameManager` is the sole authoritative game transition owner. A session pins one validated `GameDefinition` and participant identities; each accepted action advances exactly one revision and records an event. Candidates are evaluated against isolated mutable projections and published as immutable JSON state only after all legal, rule, clock and effect checks pass. Duplicate identical action IDs return their original event, conflicting reuse is rejected, and `from_snapshot` reconstructs and validates state by event replay.

`model.game.session.DesktopSession` is the durable local application boundary. It creates and resets games, exposes detached state and board projections, enumerates legal actions, submits actor-bound moves, polls clock expiry and recovers from snapshots. It depends only on the Python domain and local time/IDs; no hosted runtime is involved.

### Board and declarative rules

`Board` is generic rectangular storage for `Piece` values built from the immutable game JSON definition. `Move` represents an immutable source, complete landing chain and optional promotion; `MoveValidator` provides read-only geometric move/attack vectors. `CaptureEnumerator` calculates bounded capture chains. `RuleProgram` and `ConditionEvaluator` evaluate validated game-owned hook conditions using `BoardQueries` and `SnapshotQueries`; only whitelisted effects are committed. `resolve_outcome` rejects contradictory equal-priority terminal proposals.

### Clock and quest state

The authoritative snapshot includes participant clocks, accepted event history, capture lists, per-participant quest progress and earned quest scores. Quest conditions run only after accepted moves; speculative legal-action previews cannot award rewards. Active time is charged at authoritative action submission. The UI draws detached current values and polls timeout from the session.

### Game definitions

`src/games/chess/config.json` and `src/games/checkers/config.json` define piece capabilities, initial placement, hooks and quests; their `playable` flag is currently false. English-draughts kings declare short-range movement, unlike flying variants.

_Source: [0001-components.md](decisions/0001-components.md)_


## Immutable game rules and persisted user preferences

### Trusted game data

Bundled `games/<identifier>/config.json` is loaded by the strict `load_bundled_definition` resource reader without importing individual game Python packages. The version-2 parser rejects duplicate keys, unknown fields, unsupported expressions and unbounded data. Frozen `GameDefinition` instances provide the immutable source for generic board/piece construction, rule hooks, state fields, clocks and configured quests.

`model.game.manager.GameManager` interprets only whitelisted, bounded declarative conditions, queries and effects; game identifiers do not select executable Python rule classes. Per-action work budgets bound geometric searches and condition evaluation. The same pinned definition is embedded in replayable canonical snapshots.

### User settings

`model.game.preferences` and `view.settings_dialog.SettingsDialog` permit players to set board square size (32–88 pixels) and visibility of coordinates. Persisted preferences contain only these fields. They are validated before writing, stored outside immutable game resources in the OS-specific application-data directory and atomically replaced. The UI exposes no rule or quest editing. Corrupted preference documents raise an error rather than being executed.

_Source: [0002-configuration.md](decisions/0002-configuration.md)_


## Desktop entry, controllers and Tkinter view ownership

`chesswithquests:main` validates game selection and builds a local `DesktopSession` with two participants. `view.app.build_application` constructs the Tkinter game window and selector; `GameController` maps player square clicks to legal complete intents and submits them with expected revisions; `WindowController` owns window status and timeout polling.

The Tkinter `BoardView` renders detached board projections and selected/legal destinations, while `PlayerGameView` owns UI refresh, game switching, move-choice dialogs, history, JSON snapshot export and shutdown callback cancellation. `PlayerView` and `QuestList` display clock/capture status and immutable quest descriptions/progress. `SettingsDialog` edits only allowlisted persisted presentation preferences.

`desktop-gameplay.yml` exercises these widgets under Xvfb; publication acceptance still requires complete game behavior and real frozen native executables.

_Source: [0003-application.md](decisions/0003-application.md)_


## Documentation, CI and desktop release architecture

`.agents/GOAL.md`, `PLAN.md`, `TODO.md` and `SCRATCHPAD.md` are authored working records. `.github/scripts/generate_documents.py` produces README, PRD, ARCHITECTURE and AGENTS from approved source directories; the root README and CONTRIBUTING are symlinks. `.agents/architecture/diagrams/` contains source-derived Mermaid diagrams.

`.github/tests/` owns all repository test resources. `desktop-gameplay.yml` verifies actual local-session gameplay on Python 3.10–3.13 and a real Tkinter user path on Xvfb. Other CI workflows enforce source quality, documentation, governance, release metadata and native package infrastructure. `develop` is the integration branch; `main` the protected release branch.

`desktop-build.yml` defines Windows x64, macOS ARM64/x64 and Linux x64 packaging. `package_desktop.py` produces artifacts and checksums. `release.yml` requires verified version/source identity and all expected platform assets. Python release publication remains disabled in `repo.dfconfig` until complete application and frozen-platform acceptance are verified.

_Source: [0004-repository.md](decisions/0004-repository.md)_
